description: MATERIALIZED VIEW and DYNAMIC TABLE are QUERYABLE: a reference in FROM materialises on read by executing the object's defining query. Previously they were registered with no backing storage, so SELECT ... FROM <mv> returned nothing. Because they materialise on READ they reflect base changes, which the third test shows by inserting into the base between two counts. A materialised view applies its own predicate, a dynamic table computes its derived columns, and both take aggregates and filters like any other relation. Converted 1:1 from query/MaterializedViewDynamicTableQueryTest (now retired); the Java read one or two cells per test, which the converted tests state as whole ordered row sets.

steps.sql: CREATE WAREHOUSE IF NOT EXISTS wh
CREATE TABLE base (id INTEGER, amount INTEGER)
INSERT INTO base VALUES (1, 100), (2, 200), (3, 300)
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv AS SELECT id, amount FROM base WHERE amount >= 200
CREATE DYNAMIC TABLE dt TARGET_LAG='1 MINUTE' WAREHOUSE=wh AS SELECT id, amount * 2 AS dbl FROM base
SELECT id, amount FROM mv ORDER BY id
